newsitem.title: USA: North Carolina House panel approves food tax cut.
newsitem.headline: North Carolina House panel approves food tax cut.

text.p: North Carolina's House Finance Committee voted to cut the state sales tax on food to 2 percent from 3 percent.
The panel approved the cut Tuesday after learning that state revenues were running $219 million above projections for the current year.
The proposal, which would reduce state revenues by about $90 million annually, still must pass the full House and the Senate. It would take effect Jan. 1, 1998.
The sales tax on food was enacted in 1961 and is levied on top of local sales taxes of at least 2 percent. Critics have complained that the tax disporportionately hurts the working poor.
Last year the General Assembly cut the statewide sales tax on food to 3 percent from 4 percent. That cut took effect on Jan. 1, 1997.

Critics said the additional cut could jeopardize Gov. Jim Hunt's proposal to raise teacher salaries to the national average over the next four years, a move that would increase spending by $1 billion.

But members of the House Finance Committee said the state could still afford the cut because state revenues have grown at about 6 percent annually, adding $684 million of new revenues to North Carolina's $11.4 billion budget.
